title: Normalized derived invariants through an open normal subgroup
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on a small coherent profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $P$ use $\mathcal A_P(A)$, the category of internal $A$-modules with $A$-linear condensed $P$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $G,L$ be profinite groups and $K\triangleleft G$ an open normal subgroup; put $Q=G/K$, with its finite discrete topology. Inflation along $G\times L\to Q\times L$ is exact and has a right adjoint $T$ given by $K$-fixed sections, with residual $Q\times L$-action. The categories involved are Grothendieck abelian. Restriction of actions and forgetting actions are exact. Form ordinary total right derived functors by K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $U_{Q\times L}$ for forgetting the $Q\times L$-action and $\operatorname{Res}_K$ for restriction of a $G\times L$-action along $k\mapsto(k,1)$. There are natural isomorphisms
$$D(U_{Q\times L})\,RT(N)\cong R\Gamma_K(\operatorname{Res}_K N),\qquad
c_N:R\Gamma_{G\times L}(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(RT(N))$$
for $N\in D(\mathcal A_{G\times L}(A))$. The second is the derived composition comparison for the identity of invariant submodules $N^{G\times L}=(N^K)^{Q\times L}$ and the normalized inflation adjunctions, whose transposes restrict codomain to invariants and whose inverse transposes compose with the invariant inclusion.

For a module $N$ in degree zero let $\eta_N:T(N)[0]\to RT(N[0])$ be the canonical resolution map. Its underlying map under the first comparison is the usual map from $K$-invariants into derived $K$-invariants. The inflation map $\operatorname{inf}_N:R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(T(N)[0])\to R\Gamma_{G\times L}(N[0])$ satisfies
$$c_N\operatorname{inf}_N=R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_N).$$
These comparisons and this equation are natural in equivariant module maps and in continuous homomorphisms $L'\to L$. For successive quotient projections they respect composition: the derived inflation attached to the composite projection and composite invariant inclusion is the composite of the two derived inflations. They commute with restriction of coefficients along every condensed ring map $A\to A'$ and the derived coefficient transformations induced by equivariant maps $N\to\operatorname{Res}N'$; these transformations are obtained by deriving the equality of invariants with scalar restriction. For $K=1$, the map $\eta_N$ and the comparisons are the identity under the evident identifications.

proof.text: Apply the open-normal action-model lemma to $A,G,L,K$. Its hypotheses are precisely the ring, site and group hypotheses here. It supplies the Grothendieck action categories, exact restriction and inflation, the normalized quotient adjunction and fixed-section identities, preservation of K-injectives, and the required derived kernel comparison $\beta$, represented by the identity on $U(TI)=(I|_K)^K$.

proof.text: Use the normalized inflation-resolution lemma with that same $T$ and $\beta$. Its conjugate of the exact trivial-inflation identity is the required $c$. Its resolution formulas identify the underlying unit with the usual invariant-to-derived-invariant map and give $c_N\operatorname{inf}_N=R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_N)$. They also give naturality for equivariant maps and every continuous $L'\to L$, with the specified derived restriction transformations.

proof.text: Apply the action-topos coefficient lemma to the trivial-action and quotient projections. It identifies their module direct images with $\Gamma$ and $T$ and derives the scalar-restriction identities with the same resolution normalization as $\beta,c$. Its coefficient squares for arbitrary $A\to A'$ and $N\to\operatorname{Res}N'$ therefore give exactly the asserted compatibility of the comparisons, unit and inflation equation.

proof.text: For successive quotient projections, the tower lemma identifies composite kernel invariants and their inclusions with the successive ones. Its unique extension class $T_2(b)d$ represents both inflation arrows, proving the required equality of the direct inflation with the composite. Its identity-kernel clause gives the asserted identities for $K=1$; its degenerate cases include $K=G$, trivial $L$, and zero coefficients.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-30e71c70f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four new nodes, every cited node statement, lem-sfb-condensed-split-coset-induction, both ringed-topos composition nodes and blueprint main-20261015 direct-images paragraph (3). The delivery answers the released human re-split note of 2026-10-22. Its four statement-only unsplit nodes carry the old steps 1–4, 5–9, 10–11 and 12–14 (3043, 3761, 2926 and 2067 characters). The parent proof is a 1707-character assembly; each step cites one node. Every old argument becomes the obligation of exactly one node, kept verbatim in the report. Each node adds a resolution-level normalization: β is the identity on U(TI)=(rI)^K; b is unique with ba≃T(i); θ_f^{-1}=f_*(a); T₂(b)d is the unique extension class. So none merely restates a parent clause. The item statement, stmt_deps, lean and reviewed fields are unchanged from live. The item is not dropped and nobody else has re-split it.

Mathematics:
- Node 1: Q is finite with a continuous section. Normality gives the stable fixed submodule. K×1 ⊂ G×L has coset space Q×L with section (s,1), so the split-coset induction gives Res_K an exact left adjoint and Res_K preserves K-injectives (Stacks 08BJ). T and Γ_P preserve K-injectives because their left adjoints are exact inflations. β follows from the exact square UT=Γ_K r.
- Node 2: c is the identity on I^{G×L}=(TI)^{Q×L}. The equation c inf = RΓ(η) holds through Γ(b), consistent with the definition of inf in def-sfb-normal-invariant-comparison-data. The h-square type-checks. No preservation of K-injectives by r_h is assumed.
- Node 3: θ_f exists because both sides are R(fσ)_* (pbc derived-pushforward composition), and its normalization is valid. The cocycle node covers coefficient changes on identity topoi.
- Node 4: T₀₂=T₂T₁, and T₂(b)dz≃T₂T₁(i) is unique because T₂T₁I is K-injective. inf₀₂=inf₁∘inf₂ type-checks, and the trivial-kernel case gives identities.

Edge cases checked: K=1, K=G, L=1 and the zero ring.

Three repairable faults, all missing citations of existing base nodes; I fixed them:
- F1: node 3 re-stated lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction (action topos, the geometric morphisms p_K and q_θ, coefficient maps commuting with them) without citing it.
- F2: node 1 re-stated parts of lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus without citing it: Grothendieck abelian action categories, forgetting creates kernels and cokernels, exact restriction, inflation and scalar restriction.
- F3: node 2's b^G_h, b^Q_h and node 3's full-invariant coefficient map are now identified with that node's b_u (u=1×h) and c_J.

The fixed files under fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/ add these citations and stmt_deps. A closure check shows no cycle. No target is weakened and no SGA is used.
